note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Right knee pain with clicking during running and certain gym exercises; onset ~2 weeks ago after increasing marathon training. Pain begins after ~20 minutes (~2.5–3 miles), forced her to stop last run. One episode of transient tingling in right toes after a run. Initial mild swelling after first run resolved with ice. No persistent swelling, redness, heat, locking, giving way, or difficulty with stairs/walking. Full flexion/extension. Prior ice hockey fall months ago with bruise only.
- Relevant family medical history:  Not recorded.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN (frequency not documented). Naproxen (Aleve) PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented; patient unsure of drug class). Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented). Melatonin PRN for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented). Alprazolam (Xanax) occasionally for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented). No allergies recorded.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Training for a marathon; currently running 4–8 miles; gym a few times per week. Nutrition not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Alcohol: Not recorded. Tobacco: Not recorded. Cannabis: occasional smoking of a joint.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Not recorded; uses melatonin and occasional alprazolam for sleep. No formal mental health screening documented.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Farsighted; prior LASIK surgery. No current vision concerns recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Not recorded.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Mechanical right knee pain triggered by running after training load increase; clicking with repetitive flexion/extension; full ROM; no instability, locking, or persistent swelling; one transient episode of right toe tingling post-run. Responds to rest/ice; uses ibuprofen PRN.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Iliotibial band friction syndrome (ITBFS): High likelihood given lateral-leaning pain during runs after mileage increase and clicking with flexion/extension; no locking/instability.
  - Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS): Moderate likelihood due to overuse pattern and crepitus; pain location not clearly anterior; no stair pain.
  - Meniscal pathology (degenerative/minor tear): Low–moderate likelihood; clicking and one episode of swelling noted, but no locking, joint line tenderness, or acute twist.
  - Serious causes (e.g., DVT, septic arthritis) unlikely given absence of red flags.
- Working diagnosis: Overuse knee pain most consistent with ITB friction syndrome vs PFPS.
- Management priorities: Activity modification, ice therapy, short course of NSAID as prescribed (not concurrently with other NSAIDs), early physiotherapy assessment and rehabilitation plan; consider imaging if not improving or if red flags emerge; safety-netting provided.

Management Plan

- Treatments and recommendations:
  - Continue ice therapy regularly.
  - Temporarily ease off running; avoid runs that provoke pain or require stopping. Cross-train as advised by physiotherapy.
  - Prescription for a stronger anti-inflammatory provided; take with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen. Dose/agent not documented in transcript.
  - Over-the-counter ibuprofen may be used if not taking the prescribed anti-inflammatory (avoid dual NSAID use).
- Referrals and follow-up:
  - Physiotherapy referral placed for comprehensive knee assessment and rehab program.
  - Consider clinic visit for in-person knee exam if physiotherapy wait is prolonged or symptoms worsen.
  - Imaging (e.g., MRI) to be considered if persistent symptoms or concerning findings on exam.
- Safety-net advice:
  - Seek urgent care if persistent or worsening swelling, heat, redness, fever, feeling unwell, or if the knee locks or cannot bend/straighten.
- Patient education:
  - Discussed likely overuse etiology and prognosis; importance of gradual training progression and form/footwear assessment with physiotherapy.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Physiotherapy referral documented.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Iliotibial band friction syndrome (High): Lateral-leaning knee pain beginning after ~20 minutes of running with recent training increase; clicking with repetitive flexion/extension; full ROM without locking/instability.
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome (Moderate): Overuse-related anterior knee pain syndrome; crepitus/clicking with flexion/extension; training load increase. Less clear anterior localization and no stair pain.
- Meniscal pathology (Low–Moderate): Clicking and transient swelling could fit; less likely without locking, joint line tenderness, or discrete twisting injury.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: BP, pulse; height/weight/BMI/waist; allergy status; immunization review; alcohol and tobacco history; detailed substance use; family history; sexual/reproductive history; hearing screen; mental health screening (e.g., PHQ-9/K10); oral/dental exam; basic vision screen; urinalysis; fasting glucose/lipids; cervical screening; STI screening; mammogram eligibility/status.
- Internal contradictions: None between transcript and DDx. Patient expressed uncertainty about Aleve’s drug class (noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear history via video consult; physical examination and vitals not performed due to telehealth format.
